// Writes the GIF and BMP test files for go-media-metadata #97: synthetic
// images (flat colours, no photograph).
package main

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"image"
	"image/color"
	"image/color/palette"
	"image/gif"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

func main() {
	dir := os.Args[1]
	// A two-frame 32x24 animation.
	var anim gif.GIF
	for i, c := range []color.Color{color.RGBA{200, 40, 40, 255}, color.RGBA{40, 40, 200, 255}} {
		im := image.NewPaletted(image.Rect(0, 0, 32, 24), palette.Plan9)
		for y := 0; y < 24; y++ {
			for x := 0; x < 32; x++ {
				if (x/4+y/4+i)%2 == 0 {
					im.Set(x, y, c)
				}
			}
		}
		anim.Image = append(anim.Image, im)
		anim.Delay = append(anim.Delay, 20)
	}
	f, _ := os.Create(filepath.Join(dir, "plain.gif"))
	if err := gif.EncodeAll(f, &anim); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	f.Close()

	// 24x16 BMPs, 24-bit, rows padded to 4 bytes: the 40-byte header
	// bottom-up and top-down (negative height), and the 12-byte core one.
	write := func(name string, header int, height int32) {
		w, h := 24, 16
		row := (w*3 + 3) &^ 3
		pix := make([]byte, row*h)
		for i := range pix {
			pix[i] = byte(i * 7)
		}
		off := 14 + header
		b := make([]byte, off, off+len(pix))
		b[0], b[1] = 'B', 'M'
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[2:], uint32(off+len(pix)))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[10:], uint32(off))
		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[14:], uint32(header))
		if header == 12 {
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[18:], uint16(w))
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[20:], uint16(h))
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[22:], 1)
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[24:], 24)
		} else {
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[18:], uint32(int32(w)))
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[22:], uint32(height))
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[26:], 1)
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(b[28:], 24)
			binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(b[34:], uint32(len(pix)))
		}
		b = append(b, pix...)
		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, name), b, 0o644); err != nil {
			panic(err)
		}
	}
	write("bottom-up.bmp", 40, 16)
	write("top-down.bmp", 40, -16)
	write("core.bmp", 12, 16)
}
